advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Decide whether -h/--help should be uniformly shown or hidden across all commands and align the add_help/formatter_class choice for audit/metrics/bridge with the core factories.
evidence: src/rebar/_cli/_parsers/advanced/audit.py:20-25 builds with `formatter_class=argparse.HelpFormatter` and no `add_help=False`
src/rebar/_cli/_parsers/advanced/metrics.py:20-25 likewise (default add_help=True, plain HelpFormatter)
src/rebar/_cli/_parsers/core/writes.py:25-28 `_base` sets `add_help=False`
src/rebar/_cli/_parser.py:134 `add_help: bool = True` default
diff docs/cli-reference.md: `metrics [-h] ...` / `audit [-h] {show,serve}` / `bridge [-h]` render `-h, --help` rows while `archive [ticket_id]` etc. do not
advisory.finding: The runtime-served per-command help is inconsistent: audit/metrics/bridge factories use the default add_help=True (and audit/metrics use plain argparse.HelpFormatter), so their generated artifacts advertise a `[-h]` usage token and a `-h, --help` options row, whereas every core command is built via `_base(...)` with `add_help=False` and never shows `-h`. Users see `-h` documented for some commands but not others across the same CLI.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Derive _NESTED_FAMILY from the single true nested-dispatch command (`bridge`) rather than the whole `group == 'bridge'` bucket, so flat bridge-fsck/bridge-status are not classified as nested.
evidence: src/rebar/_cli/_help_route.py:35 `_NESTED_FAMILY = frozenset(r.name for r in ROUTES if r.group == "bridge")`
src/rebar/_cli/_registry.py:298 `Route("bridge-fsck", group="bridge", ...)` and :294 `Route("bridge-status", group="bridge", hidden=True, ...)` are flat commands, not nested-dispatch
src/rebar/_cli/_help_route.py:68-70 `if sub in _NESTED_FAMILY: return bool(rest) and rest[0] in ("--help", "-h")`
src/rebar/_cli/_bridge_commands.py:85 bridge_fsck_cli treats only `args[0] in {"--help","-h"}` as help (so behavior is consistent, not a hard regression)
advisory.finding: _help_route._NESTED_FAMILY is derived as every route with `group == 'bridge'`, which includes the FLAT commands bridge-fsck and the hidden bridge-status, not only the true nested-dispatch `bridge`. As a result help_requested() treats bridge-fsck as a nested family and only serves its help on a LEADING --help, so `rebar bridge-fsck --<flag> --help` is not served by the pre-scan.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Keep factory descriptions to a genuine single-clause first line (or have _summary truncate/take the first sentence) so overview one-liners stay short.
evidence: scripts/gen_cli_help.py:96-99 `description = (parser.description or "").strip(); ... return " ".join(description.splitlines()[0].split())`

src/rebar/_cli/_parsers/core/writes.py:114-115 `edit` description is one concatenated string: 'Edit ticket fields (--title, --priority, --assignee, --ticket_type, --description, --parent; tags via --add-tag/--remove-tag/--set-tags).'
diff overview.txt test only checks non-blank/unique, not length (tests/unit/test_gen_cli_help.py:65-81)
advisory.finding: _summary() returns `description.splitlines()[0]` as the overview one-liner, but several enriched descriptions are single long concatenated strings (no embedded newline), so the entire multi-clause description becomes the overview row.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Re-document the still-accepted --no-pull flag in the read-command help artifacts (list/search/ready/deps/session-logs) so the help contract matches the accepted grammar, or explicitly retire the flag across runtime + docs.
evidence: src/rebar/_engine_support/reads_cli.py:602: `no_pull = "--no-pull" in rest` and :603 `rest = [a for a in rest if a != "--no-pull"]` — the flag is accepted at runtime for all read arms
src/rebar/_cli/_parsers/core/reads.py:47-75 build_list declares no --no-pull, so render_route omits it from list.txt
docs/cli-reference.md diff: old `Usage: rebar list [... ] [--no-pull] [--output llm]` line removed; new list.txt (lines 1-30) has no --no-pull
README.md:423: 'Pass `--no-pull` to a single read subcommand'; docs/concurrency.md:630 and docs/config.md:73 still document --no-pull as a supported CLI flag
advisory.finding: The regenerated CLI help artifacts for the read commands drop the still-accepted --no-pull flag from the published help contract. --no-pull is stripped and honoured at runtime for read arms (reads_cli.py: `no_pull = "--no-pull" in rest`), is documented across README/docs, and appeared in the OLD list/search/ready usage strings, but the new list.txt/search.txt/ready.txt/deps.txt/session-logs.txt no longer mention it — a documented public flag silently removed from its own help contract while still functional.
scenarios: An operator or agent reads `rebar list --help` (served from list.txt) to discover the offline/no-fetch flag and no longer finds --no-pull, despite it still working
search/ready/deps/session-logs help likewise omit the still-valid --no-pull
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a suppressed-or-visible --no-pull argument to the read parser factories in src/rebar/_cli/_parsers/core/reads.py (build_list/build_search/build_ready/build_deps/build_session_logs) so the regenerated help re-advertises the flag that reads_cli.py still honours.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that `rebar -c a.b=c <sub> --help` serves help with no store mount/write, and that a malformed `-c` prefix falls through to the real config parser's exact error.
evidence: src/rebar/_cli/_help_route.py:93 `def _strip_config_prefix(argv: list[str]) -> list[str] | None:` — 'Returns None when the prefix is malformed … so the real config parser in _main_dispatch produces its exact error rather than the pre-scan guessing at a help form.'

src/rebar/_cli/__init__.py:535 `_served = _help_route.pre_scan(argv)` runs BEFORE the `-c`/`--config` override parse at __init__.py:544, so the pre-scan itself must strip the prefix — a new sequencing behavior.

tests/interfaces/facades/test_central_mount_gate_ad9f.py:140 iterates only `([], ["no-such-subcommand"], ["help"], ["--help"], ["review-plan", "--help"])` — none carries a leading `-c`/`--config` prefix.
ABSENCE: `search_files` for `-c "`, `"--config="`, `_valid_override`, and `config-prefix` finds no test exercising the config-prefix-before-help pre-scan path.
advisory.finding: The new pre-scan config-prefix handling in _help_route._strip_config_prefix is untested: no test exercises a help/overview/unknown request behind a leading `-c SECTION.KEY=VALUE` / `--config=…` prefix (e.g. `rebar -c a.b=c create --help`) proving it serves help without mounting/writing, nor the malformed-prefix fall-through (value lacking `=`) that must return None so the real config parser emits its exact error.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add cases to the dd62 no-mount test (or a new _help_route test) for a leading well-formed `-c section.key=value` before a help/overview/unknown token (asserting exit code, served bytes, and no .tickets-tracker), plus a malformed `-c badvalue` case asserting pre_scan returns None / the real config error is emitted.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that monkeypatches a route's parser factory to yield a blank description and asserts gen_cli_help --check (and --write) exit non-zero naming the offending command.
evidence: scripts/gen_cli_help.py:122 `def _blank_summary_failures()` — docstring in the module: 'A present-but-blank summary is a hard --check failure — a command whose factory was not enriched is never silently emitted.'
scripts/gen_cli_help.py:138 `blanks = _blank_summary_failures()` gates `_check`; scripts/gen_cli_help.py:174 gates `_write` ('refusing to write').

tests/unit/test_gen_cli_help.py:65 `test_overview_lists_every_visible_command_once_with_nonblank_summary` asserts the committed overview rows are non-blank but never drives a route with a blank description to prove the guard returns non-zero.
ABSENCE: `search_files` for `_blank_summary` and `refusing to write` finds only the source, no test.
advisory.finding: The generator's blank-summary hard-failure guard (_blank_summary_failures, gating both --check and --write) is untested: no test proves --check or --write FAILS when a visible command's parser description is blank. The existing overview test only asserts the committed artifacts are currently non-blank, never inverting the condition to exercise the guard branch.
advisory.suggested_fix: In test_gen_cli_help.py, import the generator module and monkeypatch _summary (or a route's factory) to return an empty description, then assert _check()/main([]) return 1 and the stderr names the blank command.

Code: `return route.group != "intercept" and not route.hidden and not route.retired`
